mohler.note: checklists paraphrase the corpus's reference answers; kept in scratch, hash here

Correctness: All required Java source files for the application are present in the submission.
The submitted project opens in BlueJ.
The application starts/runs in BlueJ without crashing at launch.
Every base task required by the assignment is implemented.
The implemented base tasks behave as specified for normal inputs/actions.
The application handles the specified edge-case or invalid inputs/actions correctly.
The application follows the assignment's required output, user-interface, file, or data-format details without minor deviations.
At least one challenge task is completed.
All challenge tasks required for the highest band are completed with a technically strong implementation.
Documentation is included that identifies the completed challenge tasks and explains how they were implemented.
All submission instructions, including naming, packaging, and required artefacts, were followed.
Code Elegance: Is the submission organised into multiple appropriate classes or modules rather than placing unrelated functionality in one class or file?
Does each class have a clear, focused responsibility?
Does each non-trivial operation have an appropriate helper method or function rather than being embedded in a long monolithic block?
Is repeated logic factored into reusable methods, classes, or constants?
Is the code largely free of duplicated code blocks that would need to be updated in multiple places?
Can new or extended features be added by reusing or extending existing code without changing many unrelated sections?
Are the base-task features implemented using reusable structures rather than one-off special-case code?
Are any implemented challenge-task features integrated using the same reusable design as the base-task features?
Does the code use appropriate algorithms or data structures instead of avoidable brute-force approaches?
Is the code efficient without relying on unnecessarily complex or hard-to-read constructs?
Is the code free from obvious poor design choices that significantly reduce maintainability in any one area?
Is the overall program structure easy to navigate, with clear naming and consistent organisation?
Readability: Does indentation consistently reflect the nesting of code blocks?
Are blank lines used to separate logical sections of code?
Is spacing around operators consistent throughout the code?
Are variable names meaningful for the values they store?
Are method or function names meaningful for the operations they perform?
Is the code organised so that related statements are grouped together logically?
Does each method or function perform a single well-defined operation?
Is each class focused on a single coherent responsibility?
Are class fields hidden using private access where appropriate?
Are methods public only when they need to be used from outside their class?
Documentation: Every source file includes a header comment with student-identifying information.
Each class has a comment at the beginning of the file describing the class's role or contents.
Each method or function has a comment immediately before it describing its purpose.
Each method or function with parameters documents what each parameter represents.
Each non-void method or function documents what its return value represents.
Non-obvious logical blocks of code are accompanied by comments explaining their intent.
The comments help the reader understand what the program or component is accomplishing.
The comments help the reader understand how the program or component accomplishes its task.
The comments avoid merely restating self-evident code operations.
The code is not cluttered with excessive or redundant comments.
